task.description: WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-0724 on branch feature/WF03-ISS0724-20260919, per ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis. Design artefact into lib/letflow/design/.
acceptance_criteria: Exact new/changed function signatures and @specs for materialize_session/5 and persist_session_questions/4
Exact sort_order computation preserving current behavior
States concretely how AC1's 'fail to compile or fail an obvious assertion' bar is met
States independent judgment on tagging vs. list-separation, not a rubber stamp of ISSUE-FIXER's recommendation
Design doc only, no implementation code

result.summary:
Design artefact: lib/letflow/design/iss0724-exam-question-origin-separation.md. Followed ISSUE-FIXER's list-separation recommendation with independent reasoning (section 1): tagging resolved_question() would widen QuestionSetResolver's public type for a caller-side concern, violating iss0722 design doc section 2's module boundary, and is only runtime-checkable, not a compile-time guarantee.

materialize_session/5 (section 2): resolved_random computation and resolved_manual_unindexed construction unchanged; replaces the concatenate-then-Enum.with_index/1 block with Enum.with_index(resolved_manual_unindexed, length(resolved_random)) to assign only the manual block's sort_order, continuing numbering from where the random block leaves off -- proven bit-for-bit identical to current output (random block's sort_order was already 0..n-1 matching its list position). Calls persist_session_questions/5 with resolved_random and resolved_manual as two separate arguments, never concatenated.

persist_session_questions/4 -> persist_session_questions/5 (section 3): arity change, old 4-arity clause deleted entirely, no overload/fallback. New signature takes resolved_random and resolved_manual as separate typed params ([QuestionSetResolver.resolved_question()] each), delegating row-writing to a new private write_question_rows/4 helper (today's Enum.reduce_while/write_record loop, unchanged, called twice -- random block first, then manual).

AC1 mechanism (section 4): a future edit reintroducing a merged list and calling the old 4-arg shape hits 'undefined function persist_session_questions/4' -- a hard compile failure under mix letflow.check -> compile --warnings-as-errors, satisfying AC1's literal 'fail to compile' bar. Scoped honestly: catches wrong-arity/merge edits, not an in-place Enum.shuffle on resolved_manual alone -- that residual case is covered by TEST-DESIGNER's property test per iss0722 design doc section 7, matching AC1's 'or fail an obvious assertion' alternative.

AC2 (section 5): lists every untouched function/value explicitly (resolver, fetch helpers, attrs shape, block ordering, shuffle semantics) confirming no behavior change. No open questions remain.
